## Why it matters internationally

Prof. Jürgen Hartmann's Sensorik laboratory at THWS works on radiometry,
thermometry and opto-thermal characterisation of materials at high temperature.
With the Institute of Digital Engineering, the group has published a calibrated
MWIR thermography system for absolute temperature measurement in laser powder bed
fusion over 500–1500 K, which depends on separately measured emissivity of the
processed material. THWS was a partner in the European metrology project Hi-TRACE
on reference equipment for emissivity above 1500 °C. Much of the high-temperature
emissivity measurement behind this work is done with CAE Würzburg, where Hartmann
is also affiliated.

## Scope of activity

- **Quantities:** absolute surface temperatures in laser powder bed fusion (calibrated in-situ thermography) · radiation thermometry at high temperatures
- **Spectral range:** MWIR InSb camera with a narrowband filter at 2040 nm (Höfflin et al. 2024)
- **Temperature:** In-situ thermography calibrated for 500–1500 K (Höfflin et al. 2024)
- **Methodology:** Pixel-wise radiometric calibration of an MWIR thermography system against a blackbody cavity and reference pyrometer, used through the scan-head optical path of a laser powder bed fusion research platform; emissivity of the resolidified material, measured separately at high temperature, converts radiance to true temperature.
- **Named facilities:** SPIT — synchronized path infrared thermography on a PBF-LB/M research platform

**Application domains:** in-situ temperature measurement in laser powder bed fusion of metals · radiation thermometry for gas turbines · thermophysical characterisation at very high temperatures (Hi-TRACE partner).

## IR-EMPOWER contributions

- IR-EMPOWER 2026: Jürgen Hartmann, “Determination of Emissivity as Basis for Non-Contact Temperature Measurements in 3D-Metal-Printing”
